% Files of the document that give a .4ht's name in \ProvidesFile, read
% with the primitive \input from the document's .def file beside it,
% which the document reads with LaTeX's \input.
% - test-ownprim-def.def reads test-ownprim/index.tex, named like
%   index.4ht. As in the PDF, the file's text is in the page. index.4ht
%   defines \printindex, which the PDF does not have, so the page shows
%   that it was read: a sentence the PDF does not have.
% - test-ownprim-def.def reads test-ownprim/framed.tex, named like
%   framed.4ht, and the document then loads the framed package. As in the
%   PDF, the file's text is in the page, and tex4ht keeps its
%   configuration of the package: framed.4ht defines \a:makeframed, so
%   the page shows that it was read, as for any document that loads
%   framed.
\documentclass{article}
\input{test-ownprim-def.def}
\usepackage{framed}
\begin{document}
Index: \ownprimindex
\ifdefined\printindex\par Index read for the web.\fi\par
Framed: \ownprimframed
\expandafter\ifx\csname a:makeframed\endcsname\relax\else\par Framed read for the web.\fi
\end{document}
